svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: iOS · Photo grading viewer · media at full size · portrait
svg.desc: Mirrors App/PhotoViewerView.swift, the editor presented from App/ProjectDetailView.swift (GradingCard's Edit pill) for a Photo-mode capture — and for an interval shoot, which opens it on its first source frame and persists the grade onto the same project fields. (A video project has no such viewer; it edits in App/VideoEditorView.swift — see project-detail.video.portrait.svg.) Not to be confused with project-photos.viewer.portrait.svg, which is the interval-frame pager (CaptureFrameViewer). Stacked layout (`stackedBody`), used whenever the available width is under 500pt — iPhone portrait at 393–440pt, and nothing else: the iPad sheet (~578pt) and iPhone landscape both take the side rail. Top to bottom: the graded image, the preview-size drag handle, the preset chip strip, then the adjustment sliders — which are always on screen. There is no Customise disclosure any more: with the picture pinned and the controls scrolling beneath it, hiding the sliders behind an accordion only added a tap. The handle between the two is the expand/collapse control for the media (`dragHandle(span:)`): dragging it up trades media height for control room, between a ceiling of 80% of the available height (`mediaCeilingFraction`) and a floor of 25% (`mediaFloorFraction`), i.e. mediaScale 1 → 0. Double-tapping it restores the ceiling, and VoiceOver sees it as the adjustable "Preview size" with a percentage value; it is drawn only while there is height to give away (`dragSpan` > 0). This canvas draws it at rest — mediaScale = 1, media at the ceiling — so the control stack scrolls: the chips and the first sliders are above the fold and Save as Preset is not. See project-photo.viewer.expanded.portrait.svg for the handle dragged all the way up (LL_VIEWER=expanded), where the whole panel and Save as Preset fit, and project-photo.viewer.landscape.svg for the side rail, which has no handle at all. The image renders through PhotoGrader.render(url:preset:adjustments:maxDimension:) at 2000px, so it shows the live grade rather than the untouched original; renders are debounced 100ms. Chips are the five built-ins (Natural · Cinema · Matte · Vivid · Original) followed by any saved CustomPreset; the strip scrolls horizontally, so Original is clipped at the screen edge at this width. A built-in chip is highlighted only when no saved preset matches the current preset+adjustments exactly. Long-pressing a custom chip offers Delete preset. NOT YET RESTAGED (2026-08-18): the editor is a black fullScreenCover with a floating back chevron over the image rather than the light sheet with the Done bar drawn here, so the handle — white at 35% over black in the app — is drawn in this file's light idiom (#000 at 20%, the grabber value the rest of these specs use); and a "Preset" state row with its PresetStatePill sits between the image and the chips.
svg.text: iOS · Photo grading viewer · media at full size · portrait · 393×852 pt
mirrors App/PhotoViewerView.swift — stacked layout under 500pt · preview-size handle at rest (mediaScale 1) · sliders always shown
